title: Deep Sea Pressure
hook: What happens if you dive to the bottom?

beats.label: 1 KM
beats.line: At one kilometer, pressure is a hundred atmospheres, crushing air pockets.
beats.idea: Character squeezes eyes shut; small 'pop' graphic appears near ears.

beats.label: 2 KM
beats.line: At two kilometers, gas volumes shrink to under one percent.
beats.idea: Character’s chest visibly flattens; ribcage lines tighten.

beats.label: 3 KM
beats.line: At three kilometers, nitrogen narcosis makes you feel disoriented.
beats.idea: Tiny bubbles form in a close-up of a vein; character looks dizzy.

beats.label: 4 KM
beats.line: At four kilometers, the pressure would be fatal without a suit.
beats.idea: Character’s outline shortens and widens slightly; pressure waves ripple outward.

description: A cartoon diver experiences escalating physical changes as they descend to four kilometers in the ocean.

facts.claim: At 100 meters (approx 0.1 km) pressure is 10 atmospheres; at 1 km it is 100 atmospheres.
Lungs compress significantly with depth due to Boyle's Law.
Nitrogen narcosis and decompression sickness (bubbles) occur at depth.

topic: What happens if you dive to the ocean floor?
